issues.quote: where `p` is one `Product` read from the products table
issues.text: In List(), `db.Products.Select(p => new ProductDto(...))` is an EF Core query projection: only the three columns are selected and no `Product` object is materialized; `p` is the lambda's stand-in for a row. Get(int id) (FindAsync) does read a whole Product. Literally imprecise, harmless at level 1.
issues.fix: Replace with: "where `p` stands for one row of the products table."

issues.quote: serialization — turning a DTO into JSON automatically when an endpoint returns it; each property becomes a JSON field.
issues.text: The definition ties serialization to DTOs, but the first misconception depends on it also working on a non-DTO: returning `Customer` (an entity) 'would serialize that field too'. I could piece it together, but for a moment I wondered whether an entity would be serialized at all.
issues.fix: Change the definition to "turning whatever an endpoint returns — normally a DTO — into JSON automatically; each property becomes a JSON field."

issues.quote: Nothing in `ProductDto` asks for this, and this lesson only looks at the names in a response.
issues.text: The previous paragraph says deserialization fills 'one JSON field filling one property'. Since names change case going out, I wonder whether a POST body must send `items` or `Items`. The sentence says it is out of scope, so I am not stuck, but the question stays open.
issues.fix: Add "— request bodies are left for a later lesson" to the end of the sentence so the open question is clearly deliberate.

issues.quote: Property names do not survive that trip unchanged going out
issues.text: "That trip" follows a paragraph about the request coming in, so I first read it as the request trip; only "going out" corrects me. I re-read the sentence once.
issues.fix: Replace "that trip unchanged going out" with "the trip from a DTO to a JSON response unchanged".
